einzeiler: The history, evolution, and current confusing definition of podcasts
kurzfassung: Podcasts are more popular than ever, yet the definition of what constitutes a podcast has become increasingly confusing. As video integration and conversational formats dominate the medium, creators examine how the industry has changed. The episode traces the evolution of podcasting and explores the current state of the format.
stichpunkte: The historical definition of podcasts as audio-only distributed over the internet
The shift toward video and conversational formats among popular shows
The evolution of podcasting through the personal experiences of the creators
The changing state of the podcasting format
beschreibung:
Podcasts are everywhere. They’re more popular and influential than they’ve ever been. But at the same time, what makes a podcast a “podcast” has never been more confusing.

Until recently, the definition of “podcast” was clear: audio distributed over the internet. A podcast was something you listened to, not something you watched. But now, almost all of the most popular podcasts have video, too. And most of these podcasts share a video-friendly format: two or three people chatting behind big bulky microphones.

You may have noticed that our podcast, Decoder Ring, does not have video, so these developments have given our team, like many other podcast-makers, no shortage of anxiety. In this week’s episode, we’re embracing our inner chatcast: host Willa Paskin and supervising producer Evan Chung trace the history and evolution of podcasting through their own histories with the medium, and wrestle with their complicated feelings about the state of the format in 2026.
